messages:
lina: FYI - running into a parity issue between REST and Python SDK v0.14 on the sampleapp onboarding flow. REST returns a 202 + async id, SDK raises an exception and does not return the async id.

aj: ugh, can you paste the error? is this the same endpoint as the quickstart?

lina: same endpoint (/v1/jobs/generate). REST response: 202 {"job_id":"job_abc123"} -> we poll /v1/jobs/job_abc123. With SDK call `client.jobs.create(...)` I get: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sampleapp/onboard.py", line 42, in <module>
    resp = client.jobs.create(payload)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/redwood_sdk/client.py", line 212, in create
    raise RedwoodError('unexpected response')
redwood.errors.RedwoodError: unexpected response
```
No job id in exception.

sam: did you check response.raw or resp._http? sometimes the SDK hides async payloads behind .meta or .details fields.

lina: yep, I printed repr(resp) and resp.raw -> SDK is treating 202 as an error path and throwing before exposing body. Quick repro attached: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/jobs -d '{...}'` returns 202 with body. SDK does `if status >= 400: raise` which treats 202 as non-200 and goes to exception.

aj: oh wow. That's a bug in our SDK status handling logic - we should treat 202 as success for job creation endpoints. Is this only Python?

lina: I repro'd with node SDK v1.3 and it returns job id correctly. So it's Python-specific.

ira: tagging this as devex severity-2. Could be a regression from the generic error wrapper we added last release.

lina: also noticed a param drift: sampleapp sends `wait_for_completion=false` in REST, but SDK uses `wait=false`. Server accepts both, but telemetry rules only log the REST param name, so Optimize dashboards show 0 samples for SDK runs. It's confusing for customers who look at metrics.

sam: two issues then: (1) 202 treated as error by python SDK, (2) param name mismatch in telemetry. Both are UX regressions.

aj: quick fix plan: update python SDK to accept 2xx in create helpers and expose raw body on exceptions (so we can at least read job id). Also align param names at the request layer (map wait -> wait_for_completion) and add a unit test. I'll open a PR.

lina: thanks. I'll attach a minimal repro and sampleapp patch for CI. Also, can we avoid the SDK auto-retry on 401 for jobs.create? Current behavior: SDK retries token refresh and replays request, which is okay for idempotent endpoints but for job creates we duplicate jobs sometimes (server returns 409 on duplicate). REST quickstart includes an `Idempotency-Key` header; SDK didn't set that by default for jobs.create.

aj: good catch. We should: (a) stop automatic replay without setting idempotency by default for create endpoints, (b) set Idempotency-Key automatically for non-streaming create calls (or expose option). I'll include that in the PR as an opt-in feature behind `auto_idempotency=True`.

ira: please include changelog note and compatibility section; this will affect onboarding sampleapp. Also add a migration note for anyone relying on the old exception shape.

devex-bot: New issue created: DEVEX-4123 - python-sdk: treat 202 as success for jobs.create, expose body on exceptions, param telemetry mapping, idempotency behavior. Priority: P2. Link: https://issues.internal/DEVEX-4123

aj: PR coming up in ~2hrs. Lina — can you kick sampleapp CI once I have the branch?

lina: will do. thanks! :thumbsup:
